facts: Regina Bateson authored the article 'Voting for a Killer: Efraín Ríos Montt's Return to Politics in Democratic Guatemala', published in Comparative Politics on January 1, 2022.
General Efraín Ríos Montt presided over a particularly bloody period of the Guatemalan civil war from 1982 to 1983.
Under Ríos Montt's watch, the Guatemalan state killed approximately 75,000 of its own citizens.
Less than a decade after his dictatorship, Ríos Montt emerged as one of the most popular politicians in newly democratic Guatemala.
The article investigates how a gross human rights violator was able to stage such an improbable political comeback.
Bateson utilizes process tracing as the methodological approach to analyze Ríos Montt's trajectory.
The paper argues that Ríos Montt's political comeback is best explained by his embrace of populism as his core political strategy.
The analysis sheds light on broader questions regarding how and when actors with profoundly undemocratic values can hijack democracy for their own ends.
